note: The Leg-Planning Playground's rows (kogaki#1764): a claim set read into one RelationalStructure, Leg Waypoints composed from its relations, judged GROUNDED; the Legs over them are derived by the runner and ask no row (kogaki#1767). A `{{copy:<name>}}` token in a row's `judgment_point` is replaced at run time by the text `copies.<name>` names in another table, from its `opens` words through the first `closes` words after them; a copy whose words are no longer in that table refuses the Trial before any Call.

sme_read_set.note: Stage 1 (kogaki#1764, kogaki#1766): the Mapper's reading, `sme_map_roles`, extended from one sentence to a set of claims. Under the Mapper's bound, MAPPER_CALLS. `reach` and `unreached` are the runner's, derived from `attains_thesis` through `relates`.
sme_read_set.judgment_point: read the claims in the input, `claims`, each with its `id`, as ONE set of relations among Roles, read for the Persona in `persona`. For each Role, define it in one or two sentences, as its `context`, as a kind of thing in the world of the Persona: an abstraction a claim's object is one instance of, never that object itself, written in the third person and naming no reader, writer or Persona. Name, as its `attributes`, the one-place predicates the claims state of that Role's object, each one short phrase in the claims' own words, or an empty list where they state none, and, as its `claims`, the ids of the claims its text is read from. Name each relation among Roles as one claim states it, as its `holds`: one sentence stating the relation over the Roles, naming none of the claims' objects and writing each Role it relates as `{<id>}`, that Role's id in braces, at least once, with `between` naming the Roles it relates and `from` naming the ONE claim id that states it. Every claim states at least one relation. Then name the relations among those relations the claims turn on, as `higher_order`, one or more, each with an `id`, `relates` naming two or more relations or higher-order relations it relates, never itself through another, `holds` stating it over the same Roles, each written as `{<id>}`, and `from` naming the claim ids whose text states that connection. Name as `attains_thesis` the id of the ONE higher-order relation that states `thesis` in the input; it alone carries `from: []`. A connection no claim states is written only as that one higher-order relation. A relation or claim the higher-order relation that attains the thesis does not reach through `relates` is left out of the article and listed as unreached; it is not refused. Write no `reach` and no `unreached`: they are derived from `attains_thesis`. Answer the RelationalStructure record and nothing else.
sme_read_set.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `roles` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id>, "context": <one or two sentences>, "attributes": [<one short phrase of the claims>, ...], "claims": [<one or more claim ids>] }`; `relations` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id, no Role's>, "between": [<two or more Role ids>], "holds": <one sentence>, "from": <one claim id> }`; `higher_order` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id>, "relates": [<two or more relation or higher-order relation ids>], "holds": <one sentence>, "from": [<the claim ids that state it>; empty for `attains_thesis` alone] }`; and `attains_thesis` -- one `higher_order` id.
sme_read_set.refusal: a key the record, a Role, a relation or a higher-order relation does not declare, or a declared key missing; an id that is empty, repeated, or names nothing; a Role whose `claims` names no claim of the input, and a Role in no relation, refused naming the Role; a relation whose `from` is not one claim id, and a relation whose `holds` does not carry `{<id>}` for a Role its `between` names, refused naming the relation; a `reach` or `unreached` written on the record; a higher-order relation relating fewer than two relations, or an id that is no relation's or higher-order relation's, or relating itself through another, refused naming it; a higher-order relation other than `attains_thesis` whose `from` is empty or names no claim, and an `attains_thesis` whose `from` is not empty, refused naming it; and an `attains_thesis` absent or naming no higher-order relation. A claim no relation is `from` is not refused: it is listed as unreached. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `structure`.

lpp_waypoints.note: Stage 2 (kogaki#1764, kogaki#1766): Leg Waypoints composed from the structure alone; the claims' text is not in the input. `serves` is the runner's, derived from `carries` through each relation's `from`. A GROUNDED `does-not-fit` re-asks each named Waypoint alone with the judge's text, up to `brief.unit_rounds` Rounds.
lpp_waypoints.judgment_point: compose the Leg Waypoints of ONE article from the RelationalStructure in the input, `structure`, for the Persona in `persona`, ending on `thesis` in the input: an ordered list of Waypoints, each one paragraph's point. {{copy:point}} Each Waypoint names in `carries` the ids of the relations or higher-order relations of `structure` its `point` states, one or more, and its `point` states only what those relations' `holds`, and their Roles' `context` and `attributes`, state. Every id of `structure.reach` is carried by some Waypoint, no Waypoint carries an id `structure.unreached` lists, and the last Waypoint carries `structure.attains_thesis`. Write no `serves`: it is derived from `carries`. Where the input carries `waypoint_you_must_rewrite`, answer for that ONE Waypoint alone, as the Comment beside it asks, keeping the others as `waypoints` in the input states them.
lpp_waypoints.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT: `waypoints` -- an ordered, non-empty list of `{ "point": <one sentence>, "carries": [<one or more relation or higher-order relation ids>] }`. Where the input carries `waypoint_you_must_rewrite`, ONE record `{ "waypoint": <its number>, "point": <one sentence>, "carries": [<ids>] }` instead.
lpp_waypoints.refusal: a key the record or a Waypoint does not declare, or a declared key missing; a `serves` written on a Waypoint; an empty `carries`, or a `carries` id that names no relation or higher-order relation of `structure`; a `carries` id outside `structure.reach`, refused naming the Waypoint and the id; a relation or higher-order relation of `structure.reach` no Waypoint carries; and a last Waypoint not carrying `structure.attains_thesis` -- each refused naming the Waypoint or the relation. A rewrite answering another Waypoint's number is refused naming it. The refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer.

lpp_grounded.note: Stage 2's judge (kogaki#1764): one criterion, GROUNDED, over the whole Waypoint set.
lpp_grounded.judgment_point: judge the Leg Waypoints in the input, `waypoints`, each a `point` beside the ids it `carries`, against the RelationalStructure in the input, `structure`, on ONE criterion. GROUNDED: every assertion a Waypoint's `point` makes is stated by a relation or higher-order relation it carries, read in that relation's `holds` and in its Roles' `context` and `attributes`. An assertion stated by none of them -- a comparison, a kind, a history, a quantity or a consequence no carried relation states -- is not grounded, whatever else the structure states. Answer `fits` where every Waypoint is grounded, with `sites` empty. Answer `does-not-fit` otherwise, with one site per Waypoint not grounded: its `waypoint` number, its `phrase`, the words of its `point` that assert what no carried relation states, quoted verbatim, and `why`, one sentence naming what the carried relations state instead.
lpp_grounded.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `verdict` -- `fits` or `does-not-fit`; and `sites` -- a list of `{ "waypoint": <a Waypoint number>, "phrase": <words of its point, verbatim>, "why": <one sentence> }`, empty under `fits` and non-empty under `does-not-fit`.
lpp_grounded.refusal: a key the record or a site does not declare, or a declared key missing; a `verdict` other than `fits` or `does-not-fit`; `sites` non-empty under `fits` or empty under `does-not-fit`; and a site naming no Waypoint of the input, or whose `phrase` is not words of that Waypoint's `point`, refused naming the site. The same input is asked again once.
